title: Multi-Variate Time Series Forecasting on Variable Subsets

problem.claim: Multivariate time series forecasting must operate when only a small subset of variables is available during inference, including after long-term data loss or high-to-low-resource domain shift.

gap.claim: The robustness of multivariate time series forecasting models under variable failures had not been studied in the literature, to the authors' knowledge.

contributions.claim: The paper formulates Variable Subset Forecast, an inference task for multivariate time series forecasting with only a small subset of variables available.
The paper proposes a non-parametric wrapper technique that can be applied on top of existing forecast models.

author_reported_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art methods degrade significantly in the Variable Subset Forecast setting.
Across 4 datasets and 5 forecast models, the proposed technique recovers close to 95% of model performance when only 15% of the original variables are present.

narrative_sequence.summary: Defines Variable Subset Forecast for inference with only a small subset of variables.
Motivates missing variables through long-term data loss and high-to-low-resource domain shift.
States that robustness to such variable failures had not been studied.
Reports significant degradation of state-of-the-art methods in the proposed setting.
Introduces a model-agnostic wrapper and reports recovery near 95% of performance at 15% variable availability across 4 datasets and 5 models.

source_observation.claim: Forecasting performance degrades significantly when only a subset of variables is available.

interpretation.claim: Variable availability should be treated as a robustness condition in multivariate forecasting evaluation.

application.claim: Evaluate forecasting systems under realistic variable-loss or resource-reduction scenarios.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported technique generalizes beyond the evaluated datasets, models, or variable-availability level.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, forecast models, baselines, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not describe the wrapper technique's algorithmic details or computational requirements.
The abstract does not report results at variable-availability levels other than 15%.
